title: How do I get started with Nudge?
intro: Nudge helps you work toward a daily step goal, see your progress and find a walking routine that fits your day.
text: Open Nudge on your iPhone and follow the setup screens. This guide covers the upcoming 2.1; the public App Store currently offers 1.3.  Choose Apple Watch tracking if you use a paired Watch, or Apple Health tracking to use the activity available on your iPhone.  Review the requested Health permissions, then choose a starting step goal. You can choose a goal even if no step history is available.  Continue with Free or review the optional Nudge+ plans. You can revisit your choice in Settings.   You do not need a Nudge account. A Watch is optional. Updates from other trackers depend on those apps sharing steps with Apple Health.  Getting started

title: How do I connect Apple Health?
intro: Nudge uses the Apple Health information you allow it to read.
text: Review Nudge’s Health permission request during setup. Allow Steps for step progress and Workouts for workout information.  To review access later, open Apple Health → Sharing → Apps and Services → Nudge. The wording can vary by iOS version.  If you use another tracker, check that its app writes steps to Apple Health.  Open Nudge again after changing permissions and allow time for the data to become available.   Missing permission, a locked device or unavailable history can prevent a reading. An empty result does not always mean you walked zero steps. You remain in control of permissions; disabling them does not delete previously saved records.  Getting started

title: What is included in Free and Nudge+?
intro: Free covers everyday step tracking. Nudge+ adds walking weather, weekday plans and deeper coaching.
text: Free  A daily goal shared across the week, temporary daily-goal adjustments, step progress, underlying activity history, history browsing, export and deletion controls, essential coaching and a monthly summary. The Watch includes step progress and Step Timer. Basic step widgets remain useful without a subscription.  Nudge+  Personalized walking weather; separate goals for each weekday; history-based plan suggestions and monthly coaching reviews; deeper insights and activity comparisons; enhanced coaching and weather-enabled widget views. Free does not show the Weather tab or make weather requests.  If access ends, your history is retained. Your saved weekday plan is preserved; when access returns, you can choose whether to restore it rather than replacing your current plan automatically.  Getting started

title: How do I set or change my walking goal?
intro: Start with a manageable target. You can change it as your routine changes.
text: Open Settings → Walking Plan.  In Free, choose Edit Daily Goal to set one target for every day. With Nudge+, choose Edit My Plan to set weekday targets.  Review your changes and choose Save. Nudge+ history suggestions remain editable and do not change your plan until saved.   Nudge+ also offers Edit today’s goal for a one-day override and Use my planned goal to return to the plan. Plan changes apply from today; earlier recorded daily goals stay saved. Missed steps do not become extra work tomorrow. A walking focus guides coaching without automatically changing your goals.  Using Nudge

title: Can I make my goal easier for a few days?
intro: Temporary adjustments are available in both Free and Nudge+.
text: Open Settings → Walking Plan → Adjust Steps Temporarily.  Choose the adjustment and its duration, then review the preview. Free uses one temporary daily goal; Nudge+ adjusts your weekday rhythm.  Save the adjustment. Use Edit Adjustment or End Now if your plans change.   Your regular goal returns when the adjustment ends. Check the preview before saving so the affected days and targets are what you intended.  Using Nudge

title: What does the Steps screen show?
intro: The Steps screen brings together your goal, progress and recent activity.
text: Your daily card shows steps toward today’s target and celebrates when you meet it. Walking time is an estimate based on your steps-per-minute setting, not a promise about how long a walk will take. Today’s progress helps show when you were active; History lets you review previous days and weeks.  With Nudge+, a walking-weather card can point to a suitable window. Open Weather for the full forecast. Availability depends on permissions, saved data and confirmed subscription access.  Finish By helps guide goal timing and reminders. It is separate from Walking Weather Hours, which describe when you want weather suggestions.  Using Nudge

title: How do I review my history and insights?
intro: Your activity history remains available in Free; Nudge+ adds deeper comparisons and coaching.
text: On Steps, find History and use the week controls to explore recorded activity.  Use the history browser to explore earlier records.  With Nudge+, open Insights for activity comparisons and consistency views. Choose the available period and move between date ranges.   Consistency can compare days against the same target or their recorded daily goals. A same-target comparison does not rewrite past goals or achievements. Missing days are not automatically treated as zero activity. Imported Health activity may not have a known historical Nudge goal.  Monthly Summary is available in Free. Nudge+ Monthly Review adds personalized plan choices. Reviewing a suggestion does not save a new plan until you confirm it.  Using Nudge

title: How do goals and achievements work?
intro: Nudge recognizes progress toward your own walking goals.
text: Progress and goal-met celebrations use the goal recorded for that day. Historical achievements are tied to recorded activity and goals; a new target does not mean every old day is judged against it. A consistency comparison against one target is a separate way to explore your activity.  Steps may arrive later from Apple Health or a paired device, so history can take time to settle. A notification is not required for a goal to count. If a past result looks wrong, contact support with the date and a short description rather than deleting your history.  Using Nudge

title: How do I choose reminders and notifications?
intro: Reminder choices depend on your tracking mode and Free or Nudge+ access.
text: Open Settings → Notifications in Nudge.  Review All Notifications and the iPhone or Apple Watch options shown for your tracking mode.  Free includes morning reminder and monthly summary options. Nudge+ adds adaptive morning and evening check-ins and enhanced coaching options.  Also check Nudge’s notification permission in your device Settings and any active Focus.   Watch mode offers wrist alerts; Apple Health mode offers iPhone coaching. Delivery is subject to system scheduling and available activity. Changing a preference does not guarantee an immediate alert. Weather alerts have separate location choices and require Nudge+.  Using Nudge

title: How do I find a good time to walk?
intro: Walking Weather is a Nudge+ feature that compares forecasts with your preferences.
text: Open Weather, then open its settings to review your weather preferences and walking hours.  Choose a day to see its summary and best available walking window.  Review the Next 3 Hours and hourly details before heading out.  Tap Why this rating? where offered to understand which conditions affect the result.   Ideal is the closest fit; Good may involve a small compromise. Fair or Poor conditions fit your preferences less well. Ratings describe forecast fit, not guaranteed safety. Check your surroundings and official warnings.  The best window and its Ideal portion are not necessarily identical. A rating can describe the weather while the hour lies outside your chosen walking hours. Walking Weather Hours and daylight preferences shape weather suggestions; Finish By still guides daily coaching.  Weather

title: How do I read hourly and daily forecasts?
intro: Use the day selector for planning and hourly details for the conditions around a walk.
text: Choose a day to review its walking summary and available windows. The Next 3 Hours describes the actual upcoming period. Select an hour in the timeline to inspect feels-like temperature, precipitation, wind, UV, visibility and light conditions when available.  Walking hours focuses the timeline on your chosen hours; Full day gives a wider view. Times follow the forecast location. Current observed conditions and hourly forecast measurements can have different reference times; read the explanation on the card.  Forecasts are estimates and can change. An older saved forecast is not a fresh observation just because you reopened the screen.  Weather

title: How do Current location and Home work?
intro: Nudge+ can show weather for your current area or a saved Home location.
text: Review the location and Home options in Walking Forecast settings.  Allow the location access needed for your chosen mode, or review your saved Home lookup.  When away, check which location is selected before reading a forecast.   Home while Away updates are manual, with at least three hours between successful updates and up to three per day within the shared weather allowance. Returning Home can show its cached forecast; arrival itself does not guarantee a new request.  Location lookup and forecasts involve Apple services. Optional Additional U.S. alerts send the forecast coordinates to NOAA. Neither service request includes your Health records.  Weather

title: Why is an older forecast still visible?
intro: Nudge keeps useful saved weather when a replacement is not available.
text: Read the update or reference time shown in weather details and widgets. On Watch, the reference can show the time without the word “Updated”; older days include a date. Reopening the app or syncing a saved forecast does not make it newly acquired.   Check the forecast location and reference time.  Open Weather with an internet connection and use pull to refresh when available.  If refresh is unavailable, follow the displayed wait or status message.  Use another current official weather source if the saved forecast is too old for your decision.   Automatic and manual updates have cooldowns and daily limits. Background updates depend on iOS/watchOS scheduling, permissions and connectivity and are not guaranteed. A retained forecast may still be readable even when a current walking suggestion is unavailable.  Weather

title: How do I use weather alerts?
intro: Nudge+ can display available official weather alerts and offer weather notifications.
text: Review Walking Forecast settings and the optional Additional U.S. alerts choice. NOAA alerts start off.  In Notifications, review Weather alerts for Current location and Home.  Allow system notifications if you want eligible alerts delivered.   NOAA is an optional source of additional U.S. alert information; coverage and detail vary. Open the alert to read available official details. Not every forecast change produces a notification, and background delivery is not guaranteed. Do not rely on Nudge as your only emergency warning source.  Weather

title: How do I use Nudge on Apple Watch?
intro: Use your paired Watch for wrist progress, walking timing and available coaching.
text: In the Watch app on your iPhone, find Nudge under Available Apps and install it if needed.  Open Nudge on the Watch and review its Health permissions.  Choose Apple Watch tracking in Nudge’s iPhone Settings if that is how you want to use Nudge.  Explore step progress, walking time, Step Timer, history and Settings; Nudge+ adds walking weather.   Step Timer supports a focused walking session with a step target and an indoor/outdoor choice. Follow the Watch prompts to start and end a session. Additional workout permissions may be requested.  Keep both apps updated. Progress, plans and access can take time to synchronize; opening both apps while connected can help, but immediate delivery is not guaranteed.  Watch & widgets

title: How do I add complications or Smart Stack widgets?
intro: Watch complications put Nudge information on a compatible watch face.
text: Touch and hold your watch face, choose Edit and select a supported complication position. Choose Nudge from the available options.  Steps to Go supports corner, circular, rectangular and inline positions. Minutes Left supports corner and circular positions.  For Smart Stack, open the stack, touch and hold to edit, then add Nudge’s available rectangular widget. Walking Forecast requires Nudge+ for weather.   The face and watchOS determine which positions are offered. Walking Forecast is rectangular; Steps to Go also has a rectangular presentation. Updates are scheduled by watchOS rather than streamed continuously.   Apple’s Watch guide  explains face and Smart Stack controls.  Watch & widgets

title: Which iPhone widgets can I add?
intro: Choose a compact progress view or a larger overview from the Nudge widget gallery.
text: Touch and hold an empty area of the Home Screen and open the widget gallery. Search for Nudge.  Choose a style and size, then add it to your Home Screen.  Open Nudge to make sure current activity and any requested weather are available.   Home Screen gallery  Small: Steps to Go. Medium: Steps to Go, Steps + This Week, Steps + Consistency, and Walking Forecast. Large: Daily Overview, Daily Overview + This Month, Daily Overview + 3-Month Consistency, Steps + Consistency + Forecast, and Steps + Recent Steps + Forecast.  Weather panels require Nudge+. A gallery entry is not a promise that every panel is available in Free. Widgets can show saved information until iOS grants a refresh.   Apple’s widget instructions  cover adding and rearranging widgets.  Watch & widgets

title: How do I set up the Lock Screen widget?
intro: Nudge offers the rectangular Walking Overview widget on iPhone.
text: Touch and hold the Lock Screen, choose Customize, then select the Lock Screen.  Tap the widget area and add Nudge’s Walking Overview.  With Nudge+, review Lock Screen Widget in Nudge Settings to choose Auto, Forecast, Steps or Activity.   Auto schedules rotation among views; when forecast content is unavailable it can fall back to steps. A scheduled change is not a guarantee of an immediate visible refresh. The operating system controls when widgets render and may hide protected information while locked.  Use the widget to open the app when you need fuller or more recent information.  Watch & widgets

title: How do Nudge+ subscriptions and the trial work?
intro: Apple manages Nudge+ purchases, renewals and billing.
text: In the U.S., Monthly is $2.99 per month with no trial. Annual is $19.99 per year with a seven-day free trial for eligible subscribers. Both plans provide the same Nudge+ features. Apple confirms eligibility and the offer before purchase. Family Sharing is disabled.   Open Settings → Nudge+ Access and choose Explore Nudge+ or Reactivate Nudge+ when shown.  Select Monthly or Annual and review the price and any eligible trial.  Confirm through Apple only if you want to purchase. You can continue using Free.   Plans renew automatically unless canceled. To avoid renewal after the trial, cancel at least 24 hours before it ends. TestFlight purchase timing and billing are not representative of ordinary App Store subscriptions.  Nudge+

title: How do I cancel or restore my subscription?
intro: Manage billing through Apple; restore access inside Nudge.
text: To manage billing, open Settings → Nudge+ Access → Manage Subscription when shown, or open iPhone Settings → your name → Subscriptions → Nudge.  To restore an existing purchase, use the Apple Account that purchased it, then choose Restore Purchases in Nudge+ Access.  Read the result. If confirmation remains unresolved, use the access-check option shown rather than buying again.   Canceling renewal does not delete your walking history. Reinstalling the app does not cancel a subscription and is not a recommended first troubleshooting step. Nudge checks Apple-verified access after installation or upgrade; availability can take time to confirm.  Nudge+

title: What if Nudge+ does not activate?
intro: An unresolved purchase confirmation is not the same as a confirmed failed purchase.
text: Keep an internet connection available and read the status shown in Nudge.  If the purchase screen shows Check Purchase Access, tap it to recheck the existing purchase. This does not start a new purchase.  In Settings → Nudge+ Access, Check Access may be offered for unresolved access. Restore Purchases asks Apple to synchronize purchases.  If a check cannot finish, reopen Nudge and try again later. Contact support if access still disagrees with your Apple subscription status.   Avoid repeatedly purchasing or redeeming while confirmation is pending. Nudge cannot verify access until Apple supplies a valid result. Do not delete the app or reset history to fix billing; developer mode is not required.  Nudge+

title: How do complimentary and lifetime access work?
intro: If you have a Nudge+ code, redeem it through Apple using the option in Nudge+ Access.
text: Choose Redeem Nudge+ Code, or expand More access options when shown, and follow Apple’s instructions. Review the resulting access status and end or renewal date. Complimentary access can be time-limited; lifetime access is shown as Lifetime Nudge+ when verified.  Lifetime access does not automatically cancel a separate renewing subscription. Review Manage Subscription in Apple’s settings if both are active. A code is not a promise of eligibility or a general offer of free lifetime access. If redemption is unresolved, use Check Access when offered.  Nudge+

title: Where is my information stored, and how do I control it?
intro: Nudge processes walking and Health information on your devices without a developer-operated health database or Nudge user account.
text: Your iPhone, paired Watch and widgets share the information needed for their features. Apple services receive weather/location requests; optional NOAA alerts also use forecast coordinates. Apple manages subscriptions. Support receives only what you choose to include in an email.   Review Apple Health and location permissions in your device settings.  In Nudge, open Settings → History & Privacy for export and deletion controls.  Read each confirmation before deleting: deleting Nudge daily/weekly history and clearing imported Health context are separate actions.   These controls do not remove all plans, preferences, saved forecasts, backups, exports or original Apple Health records. Revoking permission stops allowed access but does not erase existing records.  Read the official  Privacy Policy  and  Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy  for details and privacy requests.  Privacy & troubleshooting

title: How do I manage preferences and protect my data?
intro: Settings brings together Walking Plan, notifications, tracking mode and history controls.
text: Choose your week start and walking pace settings to suit your routine. With Nudge+, review weather preferences and Lock Screen widget mode. Changing tracking mode affects which device supplies the coaching experience; it does not grant Health permission automatically.  The Protect Your Nudge Data card explains backups. A device backup that includes Nudge can help recover selected settings, plans and eligible goals. Nudge’s copy of Apple Health history is excluded from backups; available Health activity can be used to rebuild step history.  Before replacing or erasing a device, read that guidance and verify your backup. Do not uninstall Nudge as a routine fix for missing steps or purchases.  Privacy & troubleshooting

title: What should I check when something is missing?
intro: Start with permissions, connection and the time shown on the screen.
text: Missing or different steps  Check whether the steps are present in Apple Health and whether Nudge can read them. Unlock the device and reopen Nudge. Other trackers may not have shared their latest records yet; do not replace missing history with zero or delete it to force a refresh.  iPhone and Watch disagree  Open both apps, check their connection and give them time to synchronize. Confirm both have Health permission and that you chose the intended tracking mode. Plans and Nudge+ access may arrive separately from activity.  Weather or widgets look old  Check Nudge+ access, location, connectivity and the forecast reference time. Open Weather and refresh when available. Opening the app can make newer information available to widgets, but iOS and watchOS decide when to display it. Older weather can remain visible after an unsuccessful update.  Still stuck?  Email hello@nudgestep.com with the app version, device model, OS version and a brief description. Remove health details and precise locations from screenshots. Never send passwords, payment details or a full Health export.  Privacy & troubleshooting
